subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core provider-profile pool-routing config/API now, or keep solving this through narrower auth-profile rotation, quota-bucket cooldown, and provider/probe fixes first?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested solution defines public configuration, persisted routing state, fallback policy, and session semantics that automation should not invent without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Design additive core pool routing
options.body: Sponsor a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool contract with one initial strategy, preserved session-sticky defaults, status/probe observability, and upgrade-safe config handling.

options.title: Phase narrower fixes first
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker while resolving quota buckets, same-provider retry depth, and provider probe behavior in separate narrower issues.

options.title: Defer to external/plugin exploration
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged until an external prototype proves the missing plugin/API seam and the native surface is worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Design additive core pool routing
recommendation.body: Sponsor a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool contract with one initial strategy, preserved session-sticky defaults, status/probe observability, and upgrade-safe config handling.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across sticky auth profile rotation, auth store/failover docs, and adjacent provider-routing semantics.
